summary: ARES-Health is an offline medical software built to run directly on spacecraft computers. It helps astronauts catch health problems early and handle them safely on their own. The software ingests real-time vitals like heart rate, oxygen saturation, and blood pressure, alongside cabin CO2 and radiation. Furthermore, it calculates spaceflight risks that raw sensors cannot see directly, such as jugular vein stasis and optic nerve swelling, and highlights affected areas on an interactive 3D anatomical twin. When an issue occurs, guided clinical playbooks walk the crew through step-by-step medical procedures with hard safety gates. Astronauts can also use a "What-If" console to forecast how changing cabin conditions or exercise routines will affect their bodies over time.
details:
The main benefit of ARES-Health is true medical independence. On missions to the Moon or Mars, long communication delays make real-time guidance from Earth impossible. Our software enables astronauts to make immediate medical decisions without waiting for radio signals to travel back and forth. It translates complex biometric readings into clear visual cues and actionable steps designed for non-physicians. Furthermore, it prevents dangerous medical errors in zero gravity through active safety stops, such as blocking blood thinners unless an ultrasound scan confirms a clot. The platform directly integrates realistic mission scenarios, for example Low Earth Orbit (ISS) or Moon-to-Mars Transit, automatically adapting to each phase. Radio delay scales dynamically from a few seconds in orbit up to 24 minutes during deep-space transit, and accounts for total communication blackout during Solar Conjunction. As the environment changes, baseline vital signals and alert thresholds adjust accordingly, factoring in higher cabin CO2 levels, deep-space radiation doses, and gravitational fluid shifts.

For this project, we used the following tools and technologies:

  • Rust: Built the core simulation and evaluation engine in Rust to ensure real-time performance, minimal memory usage, and zero runtime crashes on spacecraft computers.
  • React, TypeScript & Tailwind CSS: Built the cockpit interface with a pure-black OLED theme to prevent glare and reduce eye fatigue in dark habitat environments.
  • Three.js: Renders the 3D anatomical twin directly in the browser without third-party plugins.
  • NASA Standards & Data: Grounded in NASA-STD-3001 clinical limits and validated using real physiological datasets from PhysioNet (BIDMC).

ARES-Health is creative because it connects live data directly to practical medical action, rather than just plotting line charts. It integrates an interactive 3D body map to immediately show which organ is under stress, alongside checklists that interact directly with live sensor data and lock out dangerous actions until clinical preconditions are met. Finally, the "What-If" console allows the crew to simulate changes within their environment or exercise routine to prevent health issues before they occur.

It is important to highlight that the system runs 100% offline with zero reliance on cloud servers or external APIs. Our primary focus was keeping the software fast, lightweight, and intuitive to use under high-stress emergency conditions.
